details.appearance: A heavily disguised field operative whose name, ancestry, and original face remain unconfirmed. The working name Bones is self-selected and may be temporary.
details.trait: I listen before I enter. If the plan changes, I survive long enough to make a new one.
details.ideal: Agency. No Oracle, Legion, guild, god, or vat gets to decide what I am.
details.bond: The Liberated Toads and the people captured because of the war. I will not let their records disappear.
details.flaw: I trust an exit more than I trust a promise, and I will abandon a fight I cannot win even when someone needs me to stay.
details.faith: The Toad God intervened; devotion remains complicated

languages.custom: Understands enough Legion cant to pass at a distance; does not reliably speak Goblin.

armorProf.custom: Light armor; improvised protection from field gear

weaponProf.custom: Simple weapons, longsword, mace, hand crossbow, disguise tools

biography.value:
Bones — Player Character Dossier

Level 5 Rogue-style Infiltrator. This is a player-character sheet, not an NPC stat block. Bones is the operative who infiltrated Aegis Command, survived Order 120, woke in the Planar Sanctum, stole the Oracle's books, refused the flesh vat, fought a Canoloth, received the Toad God's intervention, exposed Thornbury, escaped the blizzard, met Elbow at Arunedeal, and turned away from an unwinnable Legion checkpoint.

Ledger: 7,880 XP, 23 entries, Level 5, Power 8 Veteran, Fame 52 Known. The embedded XP ledger remains authoritative for campaign progression; this actor sheet is the playable 5e interpretation.

How to play Bones

Scout first, disguise second, strike only when the exit exists. Bones is courageous without being reckless. His defining choices are refusing the Oracle's vat, dragging the Canoloth toward the cliff, listening to Thornbury instead of confronting him, and refusing to attack the Legion wall simply to prove a point.
biography.public: Public player-facing biography: Bones is an infiltrator with an uncertain identity, a Liberated Toads field history, and a habit of surviving institutions that expected him to become evidence.

description.value: Bones is a level-five rogue-style player character. Proficiency bonus +3. The class choice is a rules translation of the dossier's repeated infiltration, disguise, stealth, and escape actions; it does not overwrite the XP ledger.
Bones has no confirmed ancestry. Treat as a Medium humanoid with no assumed racial features until revealed in play.
A campaign background for reconnaissance, disguise, survival, and intelligence work among the Liberated Toads. Suggested proficiencies: Stealth, Investigation, Survival, disguise kit, thieves tools.
Double proficiency on Stealth. Bones infiltrated Aegis Command in disguise, eavesdropped at Alpine Bank, and repeatedly chose concealment over theatrical confrontation.
Double proficiency on Sleight of Hand. Used for concealed documents, stolen books, field tools, and keeping evidence while speaking to people who would confiscate it.
Once per turn, deal an extra 3d6 damage when attacking with advantage or when an ally is within 5 feet and the attack uses a finesse or ranged weapon.
Bonus action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide. This is the mechanical expression of Bones slipping away from Thornbury, leaving the blizzard, and refusing a frontal assault on the Legion wall.
Reaction: halve the damage from an attack that hits Bones when he can see the attacker. The feature represents the reflex that kept him moving after the Aegis stabbing and Canoloth strike.
When subjected to an effect allowing a Dexterity save for half damage, take no damage on a success and half on a failure.
Bones has no confirmed original name. He can maintain a working alias, but cannot truthfully answer questions about ancestry, birthplace, or original face.
Bones recognizes coercive identity magic. He has advantage on roleplay checks to resist being pressured into vats, transformations, or “true self” revelations, subject to GM adjudication.
After the Sanctum and Astral Altar, Bones has practical experience with unstable portals, crystal tethers, temporal drift, and survival in extradimensional architecture.
When a battle is unwinnable, Bones may retreat without treating the decision as a failed morale check. The GM may award inspiration for preserving the party and intelligence.
Bones fought the Canoloth while its tongue wrapped around this blade. Standard longsword; use Dex only if the GM allows the established infiltrator technique.
A brutal field mace carried through the Planar Sanctum. Its name is a record label, not proof of a magical bonus.
Bones fired at the Canoloth and missed. The miss remains part of the record and should not be erased from the character.
Negotiated from the Arunedeal camp. A practical shield for the mountain road; use normal shield rules when equipped.
A field-worn layer beneath the stolen winter coat. It is the source of the 15 AC baseline with Bones's Dexterity.
Obtained through the Arunedeal negotiation after Bones crossed the mountain blizzard. Essential against cold; not a magical item.
The core of the Bones build: cosmetics, false insignia, thread, wax, soot, and tools for passing at a distance. Three prepared identities are recorded in the dossier.
Lock picks and improvised entry tools used by a field infiltrator. The set includes replacement wire and a tiny file.
A mundane room key from the three-Ducat stay near Midgrual. It is a continuity prop and may be surrendered, lost, or used as evidence.
Stolen from the Oracle's shelves. Treat as a lore book and possible spell research hook, not an automatic spellbook.
Corvinarus's ten-page codex: Grafting ritual, Raventree weak points, Oracle warnings, circle repair, failed vats, and prophecy.
Notes about Legion credentials, the wanted notice against Bones, and Archie's 2,062-gold bounty over a broken rope.
Three coins were paid for the Alpine Inn room; this pouch contains the remaining campaign purse, not the paid coins.
